tier_reason: Peer-reviewed NSDI'17 paper comparing the AdaptSize-patched Varnish prototype against unmodified Varnish 4.1.2 (LRU, no admission) and tuned Nginx on Akamai production traces. Code is public (github.com/dasebe/AdaptSize) and gcc 4.4.7 on dual Xeon E5-2670 is stated, but optimization flags are not and the Akamai traces are not public, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Object hit ratio (OHR) improves by 47-91% over unmodified Varnish (+47% on the HK trace, +91% on the US trace) and by 30-48% over offline-tuned Nginx, with a 1.2 GiB hot object cache. OHR variability (coefficient of variation) improves by 1.9x on HK and 3.8x on US. Throughput is indistinguishable from unmodified Varnish: both peak at 17.5 Gb/s at 50 client threads in the 100%-hit case, and the 0%-hit case stays within the 95% confidence interval.
corrections.caveats: The win is in hit ratio, not speed: AdaptSize matches Varnish's throughput and does not exceed it. gcc 4.4.7 is stated but optimization flags are not. The prototype comparison uses Akamai production traces, which are not public. The baseline is Varnish's LRU with no admission control (plus tuned Nginx), not a standalone LRU library. The research-policy comparisons (33-46% over research systems) come from a separate single-threaded C++ simulator.

notes: The record's 0.66 vs 0.42 OHR (1.57x) and CoV 5% vs 23% (4.6x) figures appear nowhere in the paper text. The paper states +47-91% over Varnish and a 1.9x/3.8x CoV improvement, so claimed_speedup was replaced. All metadata checks out: BSD-2-Clause, 43 stars, last commit 2018-01-30, not archived or forked.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed FAST'21 paper with 17,766 trace-driven simulations. LRU is one of the six algorithms compared, and the quantified Cacheus results are against ARC, LIRS, DLIRS and LeCaR. It is a Python simulation with no compiler or hardware stated, so it cannot reach A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: In paired t-tests over 17,766 simulations, Cacheus C3 (SR-LRU + CR-LFU experts) is distinctly the best algorithm in 47% of workload/cache-size combinations, statistically indistinguishable from the best state-of-the-art algorithm in about 40%, and worse in the remaining 13%. The comparison set is LRU, LFU, ARC, LIRS, LeCaR and DLIRS. The best case is a 38.32% absolute hit-rate difference over ARC (CloudPhysics, cache at 10% of footprint). The worst case is a 15.12% degradation vs DLIRS (MSR, cache at 5% of footprint).
corrections.workload: 17,766 trace-driven simulations over 329 single-day production block-storage workloads from 5 datasets (FIU, MSR, CloudPhysics, CloudVPS, CloudCache) at 6 cache sizes (0.05%-10% of workload footprint), comparing hit rate against LRU, LFU, ARC, LIRS, LeCaR and DLIRS
corrections.caveats: This is a pure trace-driven Python simulation with no throughput, latency or hardware numbers, and the win is in hit rate. The paper isolates no Cacheus-vs-LRU number: its headline statistics are against the stronger ARC/LIRS/DLIRS/LeCaR baselines, and LRU appears only in the compared-algorithm set and the ranking study. The repo has no LICENSE file, so it is reference-only for reuse.

notes: The numbers 17,766 / 38.32% / 15.12% are on the page. The record's 'majority of paired t-tests' is overstated: the paper says 47% distinctly best, about 40% tie, 13% worse. The workload was also missing 2 of the 5 datasets. Metadata confirmed: no license (null, and the repo root has no LICENSE file), 68 stars, last commit 2023-10-05 (stale, just under 3 years), Python.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed FAST'23 paper that evaluates GL-Cache against LRU (plain LRU in the libCacheSim micro-implementation, Cachelib's LRU in the prototype) on 118 production traces. The code is public and CPU models are stated, but compiler and flags are not, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Against LRU the win is hit ratio, not throughput. In the Segcache-based prototype, GL-Cache has the highest hit ratio, up to 40% above the best baseline, while Cachelib's throughput-optimized LRU has the lowest hit ratio of all baselines, at throughput similar to Cachelib and Segcache. In the micro-implementation, LRU improves FIFO's hit ratio only by single-digit percent for the median trace, while GL-Cache improves it much more. On throughput, GL-Cache-E is 228x faster than LRB on average (GL-Cache-T 586x) at the small cache size, and 64% faster than the fastest other learned cache (GL-Cache-T 3x). GL-Cache is not faster than LRU itself: the paper says LRU runs close to FIFO throughput, and GL-Cache-E reaches almost half of FIFO's throughput on the Wikimedia trace.
corrections.workload: 118 production traces (103 CloudPhysics block I/O, 14 MSR block I/O, 1 Wikimedia CDN) replayed in a closed loop against a local cache, measuring hit ratio and throughput. Two setups: a prototype built on Pelikan's Segcache, compared against Cachelib (LRU), Segcache, TinyLFU and LHD; and a storage-oblivious C micro-implementation on libCacheSim, compared against FIFO, LRU, size-aware Belady, LHD, LRB and Cacheus.
corrections.hardware: Micro-implementation: CloudLab Utah m510 nodes, Intel Xeon D-1548, 64GB ECC DDR4. Prototype: CloudLab Clemson c6420 nodes, Intel Xeon Gold 6142, 384GB DRAM.
corrections.caveats: Against LRU, GL-Cache wins on hit ratio and is not faster: it runs below LRU/FIFO throughput, so the record's metric 'throughput' does not describe the LRU comparison. The 64% throughput figure is against the fastest other learned cache, not LRB, and the LRB gap is 228x/586x. GL-Cache does not beat size-aware Belady, which is an oracle. The paper's own artifact is github.com/Thesys-lab/fast23-GLCache, which has no license file and was last committed 2023-05-12. The libCacheSim copy is Apache-2.0 but opt-in (-DENABLE_GLCACHE=ON) and depends on XGBoost. Compiler and flags are not stated.

notes: The record misattributed the 64% throughput gain to LRB (the paper says 228x vs LRB) and wrongly said GL-Cache beats size-aware Belady. 'metric' should arguably be hit ratio (other), but that field is not correctable here. Metadata confirmed via gh: libCacheSim Apache-2.0, 347 stars, last commit 2026-09-26, GLCache sources present under libCacheSim/cache/eviction/GLCache with the ENABLE_GLCACHE CMake option. The orchestrator may prefer the Thesys-lab/fast23-GLCache artifact repo as a secondary link.
